text:
ops-bot: ALERT: realtime-p99 > 2.5s on /v1/generate (prod-us-east-1). auto-detected by p99-watcher. paging oncall

maria r.: on it — grabbing dashboards (grafana/chart: https://grafana.internal/redwood/latency). can someone post request examples?

sam g.: seeing spike on streaming endpoints too, tail latency pops at ~8s for some clients. 8:12 UTC start.

arun k.: quick checks: cluster autoscaler shows no new nodes added, queue depth up on model-inference pool. rolling deploys?

emily (oncall): no deploys in last 30m from CI, I already muted noisy alert but keeping page.

cheng: copying some queries — p95/p99 panels show p95 ~900ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~1.4s -> 3.1s, streaming stalls metric "streaming_idle_ms" rising.

maria r.: can we confirm whether it's model-slowdown vs infra? check GPU utilization and GC on runtime pods.

sam g.: running quick pod check:
```
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference -o wide
kubectl -n prod top pods | grep inference
```
sam g.: pods look healthy, GPUs 95% on two nodes, some pods reporting 0 ready replicas in model-cache sidecar (oomkill?).

arun k.: logs show repeated KV cache miss errors and backpressure: `ERROR kvcache: fetch timeout 2000ms` — could be cache store flapping.

emily (oncall): customer-impact assessment: error-rate remains low, but latency spike causes degraded UX for streaming customers >20% requests affected in last 5m. raising SEV to paging level.

maria r.: mitigation options: 1) force-fallback to smaller model variant for streaming route, 2) temporarily disable prefix caching to reduce cache thrash, 3) scale up dedicated inference pool (add nodes). prefer 1+3 for quick relief.

sam g.: I'm going to trigger model-variant routing to fallback-small for streaming-prod route (canary to 10% then 100% if stable). command:
```
redwoodctl route update streaming-prod --target=fallback-small --weight=10
```
sam g.: watching metrics now.

support-bot: Notified top 5 affected customers via postman template (internal), support on standby.

arun k.: while fallback rolls out, I'm investigating KV store (redis) latency spikes: `latency_avg_ms` jumped from 2ms -> 120ms on redis-cluster-1. Could explain cache timeouts.

cheng: If redis is the culprit, immediate short-term mitigation: bump cache TTL and reduce read-through pressure (serve from model directly) — coordinated with deploy.

maria r.: observation: after routing 10% to fallback-small, p95 dropped ~25% within 30s for that shard. rolling to 50%.

emily (oncall): pls keep monitoring and update page. I'm doing customer notifications and scheduling post-incident review.

sam g.: after scaling inference pool by +2 nodes (hot-add), overall p99 decreased from 3.1s -> 1.2s within ~2m. stream stalls reduced.

arun k.: redis team alerted, they rolled a config fix for slow replicas (rebalanced master/replica). metrics show redis latency back to ~3ms.

maria r.: summary so far: root cause appears multi-factor — sudden traffic burst + redis replica slowness causing KV cache timeouts -> increased load on model runtime -> GPU saturation -> tail latency. mitigations executed: model fallback, scaled pool, redis fix.

emily (oncall): current status: p95/p99 back within SLO for bulk traffic, monitoring for regressions for next 30m. filing incident page and will escalate to postmortem if anything reoccurs.

cheng: next steps for RCA: collect KV cache logs, redis slowlog, pod GC traces, and the exact request traces for high-latency requests (trace ids).

sam g.: created short runbook note: how to do fast fallback routing and scale commands — added to ops-runbooks/latency-hotfix.

emily (oncall): thanks all. I'll hand this off to oncall rotation for watch. closing page in 10m if stable. :white_check_mark:
